concepts.name: Forms of land use and the factors that limit it
concepts.description: Forms of land use (crop and livestock farming, forestry, wildlife management, aquaculture, settlement and protected areas such as national parks), the topographical, climatic, soil and other environmental factors that limit how land can be used, and how population growth creates land pressure and the need for efficient land use. Farming systems are in agri.land.farming-systems; farm layouts in agri.land.farm-planning.

concepts.name: Land tenure and land reform in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Land tenure systems (freehold, leasehold, communal and resettlement tenure), land as a national heritage, land ownership in the pre-colonial, colonial and post-independence periods, the reasons for land reform and the A1 and A2 resettlement models. Taught factually and in a balanced way: aims, recognised benefits and recognised problems, no slogans and no disputed statistics.

concepts.name: The natural farming regions of Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The five natural farming regions (I to V, with IIa and IIb): their approximate rainfall, location, climate and the farming systems suited to each (intensive diversified farming and plantations in I, intensive crop and livestock farming in II, semi-intensive farming in III, semi-extensive farming and drought-tolerant crops in IV, extensive cattle and game ranching in V), and why the country is divided into regions. Rainfall characteristics in general are in agri.environment.climate-rainfall.

concepts.name: Farming systems: mixed farming, monoculture and intercropping
concepts.description: Farming systems and practices: mixed farming, monoculture, intercropping and mixed cropping, subsistence and commercial farming, intensive and extensive farming, with their advantages and disadvantages. Crop rotation is in agri.land.crop-rotation; organic production and hydroponics in agri.land.modern-production.

concepts.name: Crop rotation
concepts.description: Principles of crop rotation (alternating deep- and shallow-rooted crops, legumes after heavy feeders, crops of different families to break pest and disease cycles, including a ley or fallow), designing a four-course rotation, and the advantages and limitations of rotation. Rotation as a pest-control method is mentioned in agri.protection.pest-control.

concepts.name: Physical farm planning
concepts.description: Why farms are planned, the factors considered (soils, slope, water sources, roads, markets, natural region), and sketching a farm layout that places fields, paddocks, buildings, roads, conservation works and water supplies sensibly. Budgets are in agri.business.budgets.

concepts.name: Organic production, hydroponics and GM crops
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Organic production, hydroponics and genetically modified (GM) crops: what each is and the arguments for and against GM crops and organic production. How GM crops differ from selective breeding is in agri.breeding.crop-improvement.

concepts.name: Climatic factors and rainfall in agriculture
concepts.description: The environmental (climatic) factors that affect agriculture: wind, light, temperature, rainfall and humidity; evaporation, evapotranspiration, temporary and permanent wilting; frost damage and frost protection; shade; the distribution, effectiveness, reliability and intensity of rainfall in Zimbabwe and their effects on farming; how climate limits land use. Ways of modifying adverse conditions are in agri.environment.adverse-conditions; soil temperature in agri.soil.temperature.

concepts.name: Reducing the effects of adverse environmental conditions
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Practical ways of reducing the effects of adverse conditions on crops and livestock: shading, mulching, potholing, manuring, tied ridging, watering, drought-tolerant crops, cover crops, windbreaks, conservation tillage and greenhouses. Conservation agriculture as a system is in agri.crops.conservation-agriculture.

concepts.name: Natural disasters and disaster risk management in agriculture
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Effects of hailstorms, floods, cyclones, whirlwinds, veld fires, drought and heat waves on agriculture, and precautionary measures: weather forecasts, disaster preparedness, conservation structures, fire guards, insurance and drought-tolerant crops. Cyclone Idai (March 2019) may be named; no casualty or damage statistics.

concepts.name: Forests and trees in Zimbabwe
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The social, economic, cultural and ecological importance of forests, the main forest areas of Zimbabwe, indigenous and exotic trees (common names, for example mukwa, mopane, msasa, eucalyptus, pine), and the difference between softwood and hardwood.

concepts.name: Tree nurseries, plantations and agroforestry
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Choosing a nursery site, raising and managing tree seedlings, establishing and managing a tree plantation or woodlot (pitting, planting, weeding, fire guards, thinning, pruning), and agroforestry: its practices, components and benefits. Harvesting timber is in agri.forestry.timber-deforestation.

concepts.name: Timber harvesting, deforestation and reforestation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Methods of harvesting trees, treating timber against rot and termites (preservative types, no brand names), marketing timber and keeping production records; the causes and effects of deforestation and solutions to it, including afforestation and reforestation.

concepts.name: Wildlife: value, classification and protection
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The socio-economic, cultural and ecological value of wildlife; flora and fauna of Zimbabwe; classifying animals by feeding habits (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores) and the big five; sustainable utilisation of wildlife (tourism, game ranching, controlled hunting); specially protected plants and animals; dangerous and problem animals and how they are dealt with.

concepts.name: Wildlife conservation and management
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Indigenous knowledge systems (totems, taboos) in managing natural resources; conservation versus preservation; poaching; biodiversity (genetic, species and ecosystem diversity) and habitats; human-wildlife conflict; wildlife legislation; the roles of government, community programmes such as CAMPFIRE, voluntary organisations and international conventions such as CITES. No disputed statistics.

concepts.name: Soil formation and the soil profile
concepts.description: Soil formation from parent rock by physical, chemical and biological weathering (with examples of each), the factors of soil formation, and the soil profile: topsoil, subsoil and parent material (horizons A, B and C), the appearance of each and its importance to crop growth. Texture and structure are in agri.soil.texture-structure.

concepts.name: Soil texture and soil structure
concepts.description: Soil particles (gravel, sand, silt, clay) in order of size, soil texture and how to find it (feel method, sedimentation, sieving, textural classes and the textural triangle), soil structure (crumb, single-grain, blocky, platy), the importance of a good crumb structure and humus, factors that build or destroy structure (oxidation of organic matter, capping, soil pans, overcultivation), and methods of improving and maintaining structure.

concepts.name: Soil types: sandy, loam and clay soils
concepts.description: Composition and properties of sandy, loam and clay soils (water-holding capacity, drainage, aeration, fertility, workability, warming), how to compare them by experiment, and how to improve sandy and clay soils (organic matter, manure, liming, adding anthill soil to sand).

concepts.name: Soil constituents, soil water and soil organisms
concepts.description: Soil constituents and the composition of a good agricultural soil (mineral matter, organic matter and humus, air, water, living organisms), types of soil water (gravitational, capillary, hygroscopic), field capacity and wilting point, movement of water in soil, and soil macro- and micro-organisms (earthworms, termites, bacteria, fungi, nematodes) with their useful and harmful roles. Drainage and leaching are in agri.water.drainage-leaching.

concepts.name: Soil temperature
concepts.description: How soil temperature affects germination, root growth, plant growth and soil organisms; the danger of excessive heat to seedlings and of frost to some crops; and ways of modifying soil temperature (mulching, shading, watering, ridging).

concepts.name: Plant nutrients, deficiency and oversupply
concepts.description: Major (macro) nutrients nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulfur and the main minor (trace) nutrients: their functions in plants, the signs and effects of deficiency, and the effects of oversupply. Fertilisers that supply them are in agri.soil.inorganic-fertilisers and agri.soil.organic-manures.

concepts.name: Organic manures: manure, compost and green manure
concepts.description: Organic fertilisers (farmyard manure, compost, green manure, crop residues), how compost is made, the effect of organic matter on structure and fertility, the role of legumes in soil fertility, and the advantages and disadvantages of organic compared with inorganic fertilisers.

concepts.name: Inorganic fertilisers and fertiliser application
concepts.description: Straight and compound fertilisers (for example ammonium nitrate, single superphosphate, muriate of potash and a compound fertiliser such as Compound D, named generically by type and nutrient ratio, never by brand), reading a fertiliser ratio, methods of application (broadcasting, banding, side dressing, placement, foliar), basal dressing versus top dressing and timing, and calculating fertiliser quantities and bags for a given area and rate.

concepts.name: Soil sampling, soil pH and liming
concepts.description: Why and how soils are sampled (principles and at least one method), testing soil pH with a pH meter or universal indicator, interpreting pH values, how pH affects nutrient availability and crops, how fertilising practices acidify soil, types of liming material (agricultural lime, dolomitic lime), the difference between lime and fertiliser, and correcting acidity by liming.

concepts.name: The nitrogen cycle
concepts.description: The nitrogen cycle described in words: nitrogen fixation (lightning, Rhizobium in legume root nodules, free-living bacteria, industrial fixation), decomposition and ammonification, nitrification, uptake by plants, denitrification and leaching losses, and its importance to soil fertility.

concepts.name: Soil erosion
concepts.description: Types of soil erosion (splash, sheet, rill and gully erosion by water; wind erosion), agents and causes (overgrazing, deforestation, cultivating slopes, veld fires, poor tillage), signs, and consequences on and off the farm (loss of fertility, siltation of rivers and dams). Prevention and control are in agri.soil.conservation.

concepts.name: Soil conservation methods and structures
concepts.description: Biological (cover crops, mulching, contour cultivation, strip cropping, grass strips, afforestation, controlled grazing) and mechanical (contour ridges, storm drains, grass waterways, terraces, gabions, check dams) methods of soil conservation on arable and grazing land, their construction and maintenance, and the reclamation of eroded areas. Conservation agriculture is in agri.crops.conservation-agriculture.

concepts.name: The water cycle and groundwater
concepts.description: Cambridge only. The water cycle (evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, runoff, groundwater flow) and its significance for agriculture, and groundwater resources (aquifers, water table, wells and boreholes).

concepts.name: Water conservation and rainwater harvesting
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The importance of conserving water, methods of conserving water on arable land (mulching, tied ridges, potholes, infiltration pits, weed control, reducing evaporation), rainwater harvesting from roofs and land surfaces, storage (tanks, weirs, small dams) and ground-water sources (wells, boreholes, springs).

concepts.name: Soil drainage, waterlogging and leaching
concepts.description: How water is lost from the soil (evaporation, transpiration, runoff, drainage), drainage as the downward movement of gravitational water, causes and effects of waterlogging on root respiration, soil organisms and crop growth, methods of improving drainage (open ditches, tile and mole drains, ridging), and leaching of nutrients: causes, effects and control.

concepts.name: The need for irrigation and sources of irrigation water
concepts.description: Why irrigation is needed (unreliable rainfall, dry season and winter cropping, higher yields and quality), sources of irrigation water (rivers, dams, boreholes, wells, springs) and water quality for irrigation (salts, silt, pollution) and how it is tested. Methods are in agri.water.irrigation-methods.

concepts.name: Methods of irrigation and choosing a system
concepts.description: Surface irrigation (flood, basin, furrow), overhead (sprinkler, centre pivot), drip (trickle) and hand watering: how each works, advantages and disadvantages, effects on yield and quality, and factors in choosing a system (water supply, soil, slope, crop, cost, labour). Simple water quantity calculations (depth of water over an area). Irrigation equipment detail is in agri.water.irrigation-equipment.

concepts.name: Irrigation equipment
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Irrigation equipment and its functions: pipes and fittings, valves, sprinklers and risers, drip lines and emitters, filters, siphons and gated pipes, and the assembly and care of equipment. Pumps are in agri.machinery.pumps-shellers.

concepts.name: Water pollution and water legislation
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Causes of water pollution from agriculture and other sources (fertiliser and pesticide runoff, eutrophication, siltation, sewage, mining), its effects on agricultural production, ways of reducing it, and water management in Zimbabwe: water rights and permits, catchment councils and the Zimbabwe National Water Authority (ZINWA), described in general terms.

concepts.name: Classification of crop plants
concepts.description: Classifying crop plants by the part eaten (leaf, root, tuber, bulb, fruit, stem, seed), by life cycle (annual, biennial, perennial), as monocotyledons or dicotyledons, and by botanical family (legumes, brassicas, solanaceous crops, cereals or grasses, cucurbits), and the main types of crops grown locally (cereals, legumes, roots and tubers, fruits) and their products.

concepts.name: Structure of roots, stems and leaves
concepts.description: External parts of a flowering plant and their functions; the distribution and function of tissues in a root (root hairs, cortex, xylem, phloem), a dicotyledonous stem and a leaf (epidermis, palisade and spongy mesophyll, stomata, veins), and how leaf structure suits photosynthesis (no cellular detail).

concepts.name: Water and mineral uptake and transpiration
concepts.description: Diffusion, osmosis, active uptake and imbibition; absorption of water and mineral salts by root hairs and their movement through the xylem; transpiration, the transpiration stream and the role of stomata; the effects of temperature, humidity, wind and light intensity on the rate of transpiration; and wilting.

concepts.name: Photosynthesis
concepts.description: Photosynthesis in terms of carbon dioxide, water, light and chlorophyll producing carbohydrates and oxygen; the word and balanced chemical equation; gas exchange by diffusion through the stomata; experiments showing the need for light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll; factors that affect the rate and their use in crop production.

concepts.name: Translocation and food storage organs
concepts.description: Translocation of synthesised food in the phloem (demonstrated by ring-barking), modification of roots, stems and leaves into storage organs (tubers, bulbs, corms, tap roots), and the foods stored (starch, sugars, oils, proteins) in named crops.

concepts.name: Respiration and tropisms in plants
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Aerobic and anaerobic respiration (word and chemical equation for aerobic respiration, sites, importance, comparison with photosynthesis) and plant tropisms (responses to light, gravity, water and touch), their demonstration by experiment and their importance in crop growth.

concepts.name: Flowers, pollination, fertilisation and dispersal
concepts.description: Sexual reproduction; the structure and functions of the parts of a maize flower (tassel and silk) and a bean flower; self- and cross-pollination of maize and bean; fertilisation in a named plant; seed and fruit formation; and the dispersal of seeds and fruits and its importance in weed spread and control.

concepts.name: Asexual reproduction and vegetative propagation
concepts.description: Asexual reproduction from stem tubers (Irish potato, yam), stem cuttings (sweet potato, cassava, sugar cane), runners, bulbs, layering, budding and grafting, and the advantages and disadvantages of sexual and asexual reproduction in crop production.

concepts.name: Seeds and germination
concepts.description: External and internal structure of maize and bean seeds, the conditions needed for germination (water, oxygen, suitable temperature), germination compared with emergence, epigeal and hypogeal germination, germination tests and percentage germination.

concepts.name: Horticulture and vegetable production
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Branches of horticulture (olericulture, pomology, floriculture) and their importance; seedbed and nursery preparation, transplanting, spacing and management of vegetable crops grown from leaves, roots, legumes, bulbs, tubers and fruits (for example rape, cabbage, carrots, onions, tomatoes, beans), and marketing vegetables.

concepts.name: Orchard establishment and fruit production
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Site selection, land preparation, planting patterns, pegging, preparing planting holes, planting and managing fruit trees (deciduous fruits such as apples and grapes, tropical fruits such as bananas, guavas and mangoes, citrus such as oranges and naartjies), fertiliser quantities for orchard crops, irrigation scheduling, pruning, fire guards, signs of maturity and marketing.

concepts.name: Land preparation and tillage
concepts.description: Reasons for land preparation, stumping and clearing, primary tillage (ploughing, digging) and secondary tillage (harrowing, raking, ridging), seedbed preparation, the tillage implements and tools used, and minimum or zero tillage compared with conventional tillage.

concepts.name: Conservation agriculture (Pfumvudza/Intwasa)
concepts.description: The three principles of conservation agriculture (minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover with mulch, crop rotation or association), planting basins and precision application of manure and fertiliser, timely planting and weeding, and the Pfumvudza/Intwasa programme as Zimbabwe's smallholder conservation-agriculture approach (introduced in 2020), with benefits and limitations. No programme statistics.

concepts.name: Maize production
concepts.description: Maize grown in detail as a crop of local importance: soil and climatic requirements, land preparation, choice of hybrid and open-pollinated cultivars by maturity group and natural region, planting time and method, seed rate, spacing and plant population, basal and top-dressing fertiliser rates and calculations, weed, pest (stalk borer, fall armyworm) and disease (maize streak virus, grey leaf spot) control, signs of maturity, harvesting, shelling, yield, storage and records.

concepts.name: Small grains and wheat: sorghum, millets and wheat
concepts.description: Production of sorghum, pearl millet and finger millet (drought tolerance, suitability for natural regions IV and V, bird damage, uses) and of wheat as an irrigated winter crop: requirements, planting, seed rates, fertiliser, management, harvesting and storage, compared with maize.

concepts.name: Legume crops: groundnuts, soya beans and field beans
concepts.description: Production of groundnuts, soya beans and field (sugar) beans: soil and climatic requirements, seed treatment and Rhizobium inoculation, planting, seed rates and spacing, fertiliser (little nitrogen; gypsum for groundnuts), weed, pest and disease control, signs of maturity, harvesting, drying, storage, marketing and the value of legumes in rotations.

concepts.name: Cash crops: cotton and tobacco
concepts.description: Cambridge only (a crop of local importance in Zimbabwe). Cotton and flue-cured tobacco as cash crops: requirements, seedbeds and transplanting (tobacco), planting, fertiliser, topping and suckering (tobacco), main pests such as the American bollworm, aphids and red spider mite, harvesting (picking cotton; reaping and curing tobacco), grading and marketing through contract or auction systems, described in general terms without statistics.

concepts.name: Crop pests: groups, life cycles and named pests
concepts.description: Effects of pests on crops; classification by feeding habit (biting and chewing, piercing and sucking, boring) with examples; complete and incomplete metamorphosis; the life cycle, damage and spread of named pests (for example termites, locusts, fall armyworm, aphids, maize stalk borer, American bollworm Helicoverpa armigera, grain weevils); scouting. Control methods are in agri.protection.pest-control.

concepts.name: Pest control methods and integrated pest management
concepts.description: Cultural (rotation, catch and trap crops, timely planting, field hygiene), physical and mechanical, biological, biotechnical (pheromone traps, resistant varieties) and chemical control; contact, systemic and stomach pesticides and fumigants and how they act (generic groups only, no brand names); advantages and disadvantages of each method; integrated pest management (IPM).

concepts.name: Plant diseases: causes, spread and control
concepts.description: Classification of plant diseases by causal organism (fungi, bacteria, viruses), effects, general symptoms, modes of infection and spread (wind, water, insect vectors, seed, soil, tools), and the prevention and control of one named disease from each group (for example a fungal disease such as grey leaf spot or rust, a bacterial disease such as bacterial wilt, a viral disease such as maize streak virus or tobacco mosaic virus); fungicides by type, resistant varieties, rotation and hygiene.

concepts.name: Weeds: effects, classification and spread
concepts.description: Harmful and beneficial effects of weeds, classification (annual and perennial; grasses, sedges and broad-leaved weeds; parasitic weeds such as witchweed), named local weeds (for example blackjack, couch grass, nut grass, witchweed) and their modes of spread. Weed control is in agri.protection.weed-control.

concepts.name: Weed control and herbicides
concepts.description: Cultural, mechanical and chemical weed control; herbicides classified as selective or non-selective, contact or systemic (translocated), and by timing (pre-plant, pre-emergence, post-emergence), named by type only; comparing the effectiveness and costs of methods.

concepts.name: Safe use of agro-chemicals and knapsack sprayers
concepts.description: Safe handling of farm chemicals: protective clothing, reading labels and toxicity classes, correct dilution and mixing (mixing-ratio calculations), precautions before, during and after application, cleaning sprayers without polluting water, disposal of containers and safe storage of toxic and flammable chemicals and fuels; parts, use, maintenance and calibration of a knapsack sprayer.

concepts.name: Types of livestock and their importance
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Types of livestock (poultry, fish, ruminants and non-ruminants), identifying ruminants (cattle, sheep, goats) and non-ruminants (pigs, horses, donkeys, rabbits, poultry), the importance of livestock and their products and by-products. Digestion is in agri.livestock.digestion.

concepts.name: Digestion in ruminants and non-ruminants
concepts.description: Structure and functions of the digestive systems of a ruminant (rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum, rumination, microbial fermentation) and a non-ruminant (pig and the fowl with crop and gizzard), the processes of digestion and absorption (no enzyme names), and the differences between them.

concepts.name: Reproductive systems of farm mammals
concepts.description: Structure and functions of the male and female reproductive systems of a named farm mammal (a ruminant such as the cow), the oestrous cycle and signs of heat, mating and fertilisation, and gestation. Birth and care of the young are in agri.livestock.birth-young-stock.

concepts.name: Birth, lactation and rearing young stock
concepts.description: Signs of approaching birth, parturition and assistance at birth in a named farm mammal, colostrum and its importance, lactation, weaning, and the care and rearing of young stock (calves, kids, lambs, piglets): navel care, identification, feeding, castration and dehorning at the right age.

concepts.name: Reproduction in poultry and the egg
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The reproductive systems of the cock and hen, egg formation in the oviduct, the parts of an egg and their functions.

concepts.name: Broiler production
concepts.description: Importance of broilers, breeds and strains, housing and brooders (deep litter, temperature, space, ventilation), feeding (starter, grower, finisher), brooding and rearing from day-old to slaughter, weighing and growth curves, feed conversion ratio, physical and financial records, slaughtering and dressing (dressing percentage calculation), marketing, and profit or loss for a batch.

concepts.name: Layers and indigenous chickens
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Layer breeds, housing (deep litter, cages), feeding (chick, grower, layer mash), lighting, egg collection and grading, culling and off-layers; indigenous chickens (hardiness, free-range and semi-intensive systems, broodiness); slaughtering off-layers or indigenous chickens, preparing eggs for market, and production and financial records.

concepts.name: Rabbit production
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Rabbit breeds (meat and fur), hutches and siting, feeding, mating, kindling and nest boxes, care of young, management practices, slaughtering, dressing, preparing pelts and marketing, and records.

concepts.name: Pig production
concepts.description: Pig breeds (for example Large White, Landrace, Duroc), housing systems, feeding at each stage, breeding (heat, service, gestation), farrowing, care of piglets (teeth clipping, iron injection, castration, weaning), fattening for pork and bacon, common health problems and records.

concepts.name: Donkey rearing
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Uses and breeds of donkeys, housing, feeding, breeding, care of foals, training and management of working donkeys (hoof care, harness sores, workload) and their welfare. Harnesses are in agri.machinery.harnesses.

concepts.name: Beef cattle production
concepts.description: Exotic and indigenous beef breeds in Zimbabwe (for example Mashona, Nkone, Tuli, Brahman, Hereford, Simmental) and their characteristics, breeding and calving seasons, management practices (identification by branding and ear-tagging, dehorning, castration, dipping, dosing, weaning), feeding on veld and pen fattening, and records.

concepts.name: Dairy cattle production
concepts.description: Dairy breeds (for example Holstein-Friesian, Jersey) and their characteristics, housing, feeding for milk production, milking routine and clean milk production, mastitis prevention, care of the dry cow and replacement heifers, and milk records.

concepts.name: Goat and sheep production
concepts.description: Exotic and indigenous goat and sheep breeds (for example Matebele goat, Boer goat, Saanen, Sabi sheep, Dorper) and their characteristics, housing, browsing and grazing, breeding, kidding and lambing, management practices (identification, castration, hoof trimming, dipping and dosing) and marketing.

concepts.name: Livestock nutrients
concepts.description: Carbohydrates, fats and oils, proteins, minerals (for example calcium, phosphorus, iron), vitamins and water: their functions, sources in feeds, deficiency symptoms in livestock, simple food tests and the importance of an adequate clean water supply.

concepts.name: Feedstuffs: roughages and concentrates
concepts.description: Classification of feedstuffs into roughages (hay, silage, crop residues, grazing) and concentrates (energy and protein concentrates), straight and compound feeds, the feedstuffs suited to each class of livestock, and making hay and silage.

concepts.name: Rations: maintenance, production and the Pearson square
concepts.description: Balanced rations suited to the age and stage of production, maintenance and production rations, calculating ration quantities, mixing feeds to a target crude protein with the Pearson square, feeding practices, and feed conversion ratio.

concepts.name: Signs of health and ill-health in livestock
concepts.description: Defining animal health; signs of health and ill-health in behaviour, appetite, coat, eyes, droppings, posture, production, temperature, pulse and respiration (approximate normal values labelled as approximate), and observing and comparing animals.

concepts.name: Causes and spread of livestock diseases and hygiene
concepts.description: Causes of disease (pathogens: bacteria, viruses, protozoa, fungi; parasites; poor nutrition; injuries; poisoning), ways infectious and contagious diseases spread (contact, vectors, contaminated feed and water, air, equipment), and prevention and control through hygiene, sanitation, isolation of sick animals, quarantine, disinfection and good management.

concepts.name: Notifiable diseases, immunity and vaccination
concepts.description: Notifiable (scheduled) diseases and why they must be reported; signs and control of named examples from each group: anthrax (bacterial), foot-and-mouth disease and Newcastle disease (viral), trypanosomiasis (protozoan); movement control, vaccination and the role of veterinary services and animal health law (named in general terms); natural and artificial, active and passive immunity, including colostrum.

concepts.name: External parasites of livestock
concepts.description: Ticks (one-host and multi-host life cycles, tick-borne diseases named in general terms), lice, mites, fleas and biting flies: damage, signs, and prevention and control (dipping, spraying, pour-ons, hand dressing, pasture spelling), with a described life cycle of one tick.

concepts.name: Internal parasites of livestock
concepts.description: Roundworms, tapeworms and liver fluke: the life cycle of a roundworm described in words, symptoms, the damage they cause, and prevention and control (dosing, rotational grazing, hygiene, controlling intermediate hosts such as snails).

concepts.name: Cell division: mitosis and meiosis
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Chromosomes in the nucleus, the stages of mitosis and meiosis in outline, the differences between them and their importance in growth and in producing gametes, and how the environment affects the expression of genes. Inheritance is in agri.breeding.monohybrid.

concepts.name: Monohybrid inheritance
concepts.description: Chromosome, gene, allele, homozygous, heterozygous, dominant, recessive, genotype and phenotype; genetic diagrams for monohybrid crosses giving 3:1 and 1:1 ratios; the test cross; predicting results; and the importance of genotype and phenotype in animal and plant breeding.

concepts.name: Crop improvement and hybrid maize
concepts.description: Why crops are bred (yield, disease resistance, hardiness, quality), artificial selection, open and controlled pollination, heterosis (hybrid vigour), producing single-cross, double-cross and three-way hybrids of maize, why hybrid seed must be bought each season, and the difference between selective crop breeding and genetically modified crops.

concepts.name: Livestock breeding and artificial insemination
concepts.description: Why livestock are bred, effects of the environment on breeding, selecting animals for breeding (performance, records, conformation), artificial selection, systems of breeding (inbreeding, line breeding, cross-breeding, upgrading) with advantages and disadvantages, and the benefits and limitations of artificial insemination.

concepts.name: Grazing land vegetation and improved pastures
concepts.description: Cambridge only. The vegetation of grazing lands (grasses, legumes and browse) and its value to livestock, and how improved pastures are established (land preparation, choice of grass and legume species, sowing, fertilising, weed control and first grazing).

concepts.name: Grazing systems, stocking rate and veld management
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Rotational grazing, paddock grazing, zero grazing, enclosed and unenclosed, intensive and extensive grazing systems; stocking rate and carrying capacity (with calculations), the dangers of overstocking, bush control and the use and misuse of fire; how fencing and rotational grazing improve pasture use.

concepts.name: Tillage implements: parts, adjustment and maintenance
concepts.description: Mouldboard plough (parts and their functions), disc plough, cultivator, harrow, planter and ridger (ox-, donkey- or tractor-drawn): their uses, adjusting depth and width of cut, and routine maintenance and storage.

concepts.name: Farm mechanisation
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Advantages and disadvantages of farm mechanisation (timeliness, labour, cost, soil compaction, unemployment), animal draught compared with tractors, and choosing the level of mechanisation for a farm.

concepts.name: Farm tools: use and maintenance
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Use, safe handling and maintenance of the saw, hammer, screwdriver, file, spanner, sprayers and hand tools for cultivation (hoe, spade, fork, rake, pick, slasher). Knapsack sprayer calibration is in agri.protection.agrochemicals.

concepts.name: Harnesses for draught animals
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Types of yokes (head and withers yokes) and their parts, breast-band and collar harnesses, the characteristics of wood and other materials used, making simple harnesses from local materials and harnessing cattle and donkeys correctly.

concepts.name: Appropriate technology: irrigation pumps and shellers
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Parts and working principles of hand-operated and power-driven irrigation pumps (for example treadle, piston and centrifugal pumps) and their routine maintenance; parts, functions and operating principles of maize and groundnut shellers and their correct use.

concepts.name: Fences: types, materials and treatment
concepts.description: Purposes of fencing; types of fence (barbed wire, plain wire, woven or mesh, electric, live hedges and windbreaks) and their uses; fencing materials and tools; treating wooden posts against rot and termites and protecting metal (preservative types, no brand names); advantages and disadvantages of materials. Construction is in agri.structures.fence-construction.

concepts.name: Fence construction, anchors and fencing calculations
concepts.description: Fence specifications (spacing of posts and strands), methods of constructing a fence, anchors and straining posts (types with advantages and disadvantages), maintenance, and calculating the posts, droppers and wire needed for a given perimeter and their cost.

concepts.name: Farm buildings and livestock housing
concepts.description: Properties (durability, strength, fire, termite and temperature resistance, cost) and uses of wood, concrete blocks, bricks, stone, metal, earth and thatch; requirements of suitable livestock housing (ventilation, drainage, space, light, hygiene, security); designing and drawing plans of livestock buildings and calculating their costs and cost effectiveness.

concepts.name: Farm roads
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Factors in siting a farm road, siting equipment, features of a well-sited road and their dimensions (camber, side drains, mitre drains, culverts), materials and construction, and the repair and maintenance of farm roads.

concepts.name: Farm water supplies
concepts.description: Cambridge only. Sources of water for people, livestock and irrigation, water treatment by settling and filtration, constructing storage dams that resist water pressure (which increases with depth), storage tanks, distributing water through pipes and simple plumbing (joining plastic pipe, fitting tap washers).

concepts.name: Farm records
concepts.description: Importance of farm records; physical records (diary of events, inventory, production, livestock, crop and labour records) and financial records (receipts, cash book); keeping records for a school agricultural project.

concepts.name: Profit and loss account for a farm enterprise
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Income and expenditure of a farm enterprise, the functions of a profit and loss account, and preparing a simple profit and loss account and calculating profit or loss for a school or farm enterprise.

concepts.name: Farm choices, opportunity cost, demand, supply and price
concepts.description: Opportunities in the agriculture industry, the factors influencing farmers' choices of enterprises, opportunity cost, the laws of demand and supply, interpreting demand and supply schedules and curves (described in words and tables), and how the market price of agricultural commodities is determined.

concepts.name: The law of diminishing returns
concepts.description: The law of diminishing returns, interpreting it from tables and graphs of input and output (total, average and marginal product), and its implications for decisions on fertiliser, feed, labour and other inputs in agriculture.

concepts.name: Risk, uncertainty and decision making in farming
concepts.description: The difference between risk and uncertainty, risks farmers face (weather, pests and diseases, prices, theft, policy), ways of reducing their effects (diversification, insurance, irrigation, contracts, savings), the importance of decision making, economic factors in decisions and the steps in making a farm decision.

concepts.name: Farm budgets and gross margins
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. The importance of budgeting in farming, sources of information, calculating the gross margin of an enterprise (gross output minus variable costs, per hectare or per head), and preparing partial and whole-farm budgets.

concepts.name: Agricultural marketing
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Functions of marketing (assembling, grading, processing and value addition, packaging, storage, transport, financing, selling) and factors affecting the marketing of farm produce; controlled and uncontrolled, formal and informal markets for major crops and livestock in Zimbabwe; and marketing legislation for agricultural produce (statutory marketing bodies and contract farming named in general terms, with how the rules have changed).

concepts.name: Agricultural co-operatives
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only. Principles of co-operatives, how a co-operative is formed, types of agricultural co-operatives (producer, marketing, supply, savings and credit), their benefits and the problems they face.
